Marathon Petroleum bounced back 4.6% today after a brutal nine-day slide that wiped 17% off the stock, rebounding from $372.74 to $389.88. The timing aligns with news that the midterm elections produced a "blue wave" rejection of Trump and the GOP—a shift that markets read as reducing the risk of aggressive military action against Iran. Since a significant chunk of global crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz (which Iran can disrupt), any de-escalation in U.S.-Iran tensions eases supply fears that have been hammering refiners like Marathon, even though refineries are currently running at a healthy 94.5% utilization.

The rebound also comes as oil prices stabilized: U.S. crude had been under pressure, trading at $99.64 today versus the broader geopolitical risk that characterized the prior week. Refiners' margins depend heavily on the spread between crude costs and finished fuel prices—when geopolitical risk spikes crude up without a matching jump in gasoline or diesel demand, refiner profits compress. A political outcome that reduces strike risk gives refiners breathing room, even if it simultaneously means less tailwind from renewable energy support in Congress going forward.
